opportunities.eligibility_summary: Call 11 is open 9 Jul–10 Sep 2026 14:00 CEST. opportunities.next_action: Urgent: identify/confirm an innovative SME lead and second-country partner; define a 24–36 month commercial R&D concept and partner budgets; for a Portuguese lead/partner, pair with MPr-2026-4 and verify national documents before the 10 Sep Eurostars deadline.

opportunities.name: Digital solutions for regulatory compliance through data
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU Member States and Digital Europe associated eligible countries
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: national and EU authorities; regulatory agencies; public and private entities; companies; compliance-data providers; data-sharing organisations; universities and other eligible applicants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Topic DIGITAL-2026-AI-DATA-10-COMPLIANCE. Call budget EUR 8.5m; projects normally 24 months; proposals require at least 3 independent beneficiaries from 3 different eligible countries. The call supports automated and trusted sharing of compliance data, privacy-preserving technologies, interoperability, data governance and open-source digital solutions. Submission deadline is 1 Oct 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time.
opportunities.project_fit: Strong fit for the broader web/app/AI/data capability if framed around a real regulatory-reporting use case rather than CCR itself. A Portuguese/EU IT company can contribute as technical beneficiary, co-developer or technical WP lead alongside a regulator/data-holder/use-case owner.
opportunities.recommended_role: technical beneficiary; software/data work-package lead; AI/data co-developer
opportunities.next_action: Use the now-open submission phase to identify one regulatory/data-holder use case plus two eligible-country partners; prioritise partners with environmental, manufacturing, healthcare, energy or other measurable compliance burdens. Decide go/no-go by 31 Aug before drafting.

opportunities.name: EU audio reporting 2026
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: legal entities active in news media or media; public or private bodies; single applicant or consortium
opportunities.eligibility_summary: The 2026 call has EUR 4.5m available, up to 95% co-financing and closes 7 Sep 2026. It supports independent European audio reporting and cross-border distribution. Eligible activities include technical/editorial workflows, development or maintenance of digital delivery/distribution systems, websites/tools, and data studies/audience measurement. The Commission published updated Q&A on 21 Aug 2026.
opportunities.project_fit: Not a direct CCR grant, but potentially relevant to the news-analysis application and broader platform/data capability inside a media-led proposal. Proceed only with a credible EU media applicant or consortium that needs technical delivery, multilingual tooling, analytics or news-analysis infrastructure.
opportunities.recommended_role: technical platform partner; data/analytics partner; digital distribution co-developer
opportunities.next_action: Because the deadline is 7 Sep, make a rapid go/no-go: contact only warm or clearly eligible EU media organisations already capable of producing audio in multiple EU languages; do not cold-build a consortium from scratch.

opportunities.name: ITEA Call 2026 – software innovation
opportunities.cofunding_rate: Portugal: up to 80% startup/small company; up to 55% midcap; ENESII up to 85%; Lisbon cap 40%
opportunities.eligible_countries: Austria; Belgium; Canada; Estonia; Finland; France; Germany; Hungary; Ireland; Israel; Lithuania; Luxembourg; Netherlands; Poland; Portugal; Singapore; Slovakia; South Africa; South Korea; Spain; Sweden; Türkiye; United Kingdom
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: industry-led international R&D consortia; companies; research organisations and universities subject to national rules
opportunities.language_environments: English; Portuguese; Russian; Ukrainian; Hebrew validation possible
opportunities.eligibility_summary: ITEA Call 2026 opens 15 Sep 2026. Project Outline deadline is 2 Nov 2026 at 17:00 CET; Full Project Proposal deadline is 11 Feb 2027 at 17:00 CET. ITEA is the Eureka Cluster on software innovation. Portugal has an open budget: startup/small companies up to 80%, midcaps up to 55%, universities/research organisations up to 85%, while Lisbon investments are capped at 40%; large companies are not funded. Portuguese projects may not exceed 36 months, must include at least one company, involve technological risk and benefit all partners. After a Eureka label, Portuguese entities apply to MPr-2026-04 for national funding.
opportunities.project_fit: Very strong fit for the broader software/AI/data profile. CCR, news-analysis and Faking News can be demonstrators inside a genuinely novel software platform project; ITEA also explicitly spans Smart Communities and Safety & Security. Better route than forcing these products into a purely media-literacy call.
opportunities.recommended_role: Portuguese SME technical beneficiary; software/AI work-package lead; international product co-developer
opportunities.next_action: Prepare a concise ITEA project idea and partner profile before the 15–17 Sep ITEA Project Outline Days; use ANI/Eureka matchmaking to identify 2–4 industrial partners and confirm final ITEA consortium composition rules before PO submission.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open 1 Jul–26 Oct 2026, deadline 23:59 CET. Portugal has an open budget: startup/small companies up to 80%, midcaps up to 55%, universities/research organisations up to 85%, Lisbon capped at 40%, and large companies are not funded; Portuguese companies need at least 15% financial autonomy or, if under one year old, equity capacity of at least 20% of eligible expenses.
opportunities.project_fit: Good route when the broader AI/data/software platform can be tied to advanced communications, distributed information systems, trusted digital services or cybersecurity. Less direct than ITEA for CCR itself, but a Portuguese IT company can be a funded technical beneficiary with a real product R&D role.
opportunities.recommended_role: Portuguese SME technical beneficiary; AI/data/software co-developer; technical work-package lead
opportunities.next_action: Search CELTIC brokerage for a consortium needing AI/data/software capability; pursue only if there is a credible communications/digital-infrastructure use case rather than stretching CCR to fit.

opportunities.name: Innowwide Call 5 – market feasibility projects
opportunities.programme: European Partnership on Innovative SMEs / Innowwide
opportunities.eligible_countries: Applicant: EU Member States plus Iceland, Israel, Norway, Switzerland, Türkiye and United Kingdom; target market must be in Africa, Americas, Asia or Oceania
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: legally constituted innovative SME established at least two years by 1 Dec 2026; no prior Innowwide funding in 2022–2025; one independent local counterpart in target country as main subcontractor
opportunities.language_environments: English application; target-market language validation possible
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Call opens 1 Oct and closes 1 Dec 2026 at 14:00 CET. Budget EUR 4.2m for 70 projects; fixed EUR 60k grant per project at max 70% support, so minimum eligible project cost is EUR 86k. Project duration is six months. Applicant must be an eligible innovative SME legally established for at least two years by the deadline and must not have received previous Innowwide funding. A local independent counterpart in the selected target country is mandatory as main subcontractor; innovation must be civil and at TRL 4–8 in the target country.
opportunities.project_fit: Excellent route for a mature EU/Portuguese IT SME to validate CCR, news-analysis, Faking News or another AI/data/web product in a non-European target market without building a full grant consortium. Particularly useful for market/technical/legal validation in the Americas, Asia, Africa or Oceania with a local customer, research provider or technology partner.
opportunities.recommended_role: single SME applicant with local market-validation subcontractor
opportunities.next_action: Check whether the intended applicant company was incorporated on or before 1 Dec 2024 and has no previous Innowwide award; if eligible, select one target market and local counterpart by mid-September and prepare the market-feasibility workplan before the 29 Sep applicant webinar.

opportunities.cofunding_rate: up to 60%; Lisbon 40%; Algarve 50%; regional-aid caps apply
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: micro, small and medium enterprises with organised accounting; operation located at beneficiary establishment
opportunities.eligibility_summary: MPr-2026-6 supports individual productive-investment operations by SMEs that create a new establishment, expand capacity, diversify into products/services not previously offered, or fundamentally change the production/service-delivery process. The 27 Aug 2026 republication clarified aid rates for Médio Tejo and Alentejo Litoral, revised the base rate for micro/small companies in low-density territories, clarified preparatory-work eligibility and corrected merit scoring. Global allocation is EUR 182.5m; call closes 30 Sep 2026 at 17:00. Regional programme maxima are 60% in Norte/Centro/Alentejo, 40% Lisboa and 50% Algarve, subject to regional-aid-map caps. Eligible investment must be at least EUR 300k where the regional programme applies that threshold; exact minimum should be checked for the intended location before filing.

It is not an R&D grant and should not be used merely to fund ordinary development salaries. Best fit is a real establishment/capacity/diversification investment around an internationalisable software or AI product business.
opportunities.recommended_role: Portuguese SME single applicant; productive-investment beneficiary
opportunities.next_action: If a Portuguese SME/establishment can meet the investment threshold, identify its NUTS region and whether the planned operation is new establishment, capacity expansion or diversification; then model eligible capex/software/services and aid rate under the 27 Aug republication before 30 Sep.

opportunities.name: EFCSN Database Grants – European shared fact-check database
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU or Digital Europe associated countries; editorial focus on Council of Europe country, Kosovo, Belarus or Russia
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: EFCSN-certified fact-checking legal entities or fact-checking teams/units; for-profit or non-profit; average at least four human-authored fact-checks per month
opportunities.language_environments: European multilingual; Russian explicitly possible through eligible editorial focus
opportunities.eligibility_summary: FACTEUR Database Grants have a total call budget of EUR 860k, maximum EUR 70k per project, 50% funding and 24-month duration. Single applicants only. Applicant must be an EFCSN-certified fact-checking organisation/team, publish at least four human-authored fact-checks per month, and connect editorial systems to the shared database. Eligible costs include personnel and technical personnel; subcontracting is capped at 15%; indirect costs are 10%. Payment is 40% on grant signature, 30% after interim approval and 30% after final approval. Deadline 6 Sep 2026 at 23:59.
opportunities.project_fit: Not a direct grant for a generic IT company or CCR alone. Highly relevant through an eligible fact-checking partner such as a certified newsroom: CCR/data tooling could support ingestion, AI-metadata review or technical integration, but subcontracting is capped at 15%. Strategic value is partner relationship and access to the shared European fact-check data infrastructure rather than a large technical contract.
opportunities.recommended_role: technical subcontractor/data-integration partner to an eligible EFCSN-certified fact-checker
opportunities.next_action: Immediately identify whether an existing fact-checking partner is EFCSN-certified and already applying; offer a narrowly scoped database/API/metadata integration contribution that stays within the 15% subcontracting ceiling. Do not attempt a standalone CCR application.

opportunities.name: Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator – Call 5
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU Member States; Iceland; Israel; Norway; Switzerland; Türkiye; United Kingdom
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: single startup, SME or small mid-cap meeting the Eurostars-3 completion criterion
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Call 5 opened 31 Aug 2026 at 09:00 CEST and closes 25 Sep 2026 at 14:00 CEST. Applicant must be a single startup, SME or small mid-cap established in an eligible country; must have successfully completed a Eurostars-3 project after 25 Sep 2024 or be participating in a Eurostars-3 project finishing before 25 Mar 2027; the business concept must result from that Eurostars-3 project; applicant must own or have rights to the underlying IP. Application has six sections plus an English pitch deck of up to 10 slides. Up to 11 applicants can receive a GO to submit directly at the EIC Accelerator full-proposal stage. The Fast Track itself is an access route, not a standalone grant award. Evaluation covers deep-tech/breakthrough nature, completed TRL 5/current TRL 6, IP strategy and market opportunity. Eureka is holding an applicant briefing webinar on 31 Aug 2026.
opportunities.project_fit: Strategically relevant as a downstream route if CCR or a broader AI/data product is first funded through Eurostars-3 and reaches TRL 6. Not currently actionable unless the applicant company already has a qualifying Eurostars-3 project.
opportunities.recommended_role: future single-company EIC Accelerator applicant after qualifying Eurostars-3 project
opportunities.next_action: Check company history for any qualifying Eurostars-3 project; if none, keep as a downstream design constraint for Eurostars proposals rather than spending application effort on Call 5.

opportunities.name: UK-Singapore Collaborative R&D 2026
opportunities.cofunding_rate: UK: up to 70% small, 60% medium, 50% large; Singapore: up to 70% of project costs
opportunities.eligible_countries: United Kingdom; Singapore; non-funded international organisations may participate
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: UK registered business lead; UK businesses, academics and RTOs as funded partners; at least one independent Singapore business registered and operating in Singapore with at least 30% local equity held by Singapore citizens/PRs and financial capacity to complete the project; EU and other non-UK organisations may participate only as non-funded partners under the UK competition
opportunities.language_environments: English; multilingual validation possible as project activity
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open 24 Aug–16 Dec 2026. UK submission closes 16 Dec at 11:00 UK time; Singapore submission closes 16 Dec at 18:00 UTC+8. Innovate UK has up to GBP 3m total; UK grant request per project must be GBP 100k–900k. Projects last 24–36 months, start no earlier than 1 May 2027 and end by 30 Apr 2030. A UK registered business of any size must lead and collaborate with at least one non-linked Singapore registered business. Singapore companies can receive support up to 70% of project costs and must be registered/operating in Singapore with at least 30% local equity held by Singapore citizens/PRs. No country or partner may exceed 70% of total project cost. EU and other non-UK organisations may participate as non-funded partners and work from their home countries. Under the UK competition, subcontractors are limited to no more than 20% of eligible UK participation costs and must be from the UK.
opportunities.project_fit: Good broader technical route if a UK business and eligible Singapore business are available. CCR/news-analysis/Faking News can serve as a demonstrator if framed as genuine industrial R&D in AI/digital technologies with commercial exploitation. A Portuguese/EU IT company can contribute only as a self-funded international partner under the Innovate UK side, so participation is attractive only if the technical/IP/commercial role justifies that cost or another lawful funding route covers it.
opportunities.recommended_role: UK business lead; eligible Singapore business co-lead; Portuguese/EU company as non-funded international technology co-developer
opportunities.next_action: Use the prepared partner-search pack to identify a UK business lead and eligible non-linked Singapore business; attend/review the 27 Aug briefing and matchmaking route, then decide whether a self-funded Portuguese/EU technical role has sufficient IP/commercial value.

opportunities.name: Ações Coletivas – Transferência do conhecimento científico e tecnológico
opportunities.eligible_entity_types: Recognised Collaborative Laboratories (CoLAB) and Technology and Innovation Centres (CTI) only; IT companies are not direct beneficiaries
opportunities.language_environments: Portuguese,English; multilingual validation/tooling can be proposed where it serves the collective action
opportunities.eligibility_summary: COMPETE2030-2026-7 is open 12 Aug–15 Oct 2026 17:00. Total FEDER budget EUR 45 million; max co-financing 85%. Only formally recognised CoLABs and CTIs in Norte, Centro and Alentejo can apply. Individual operations must have EUR 350k–500k eligible investment. Co-promotion operations require EUR 350k–1.2m eligible investment per co-promoter and at least EUR 1.2m per operation. Results must be collective, broadly accessible and not confer a direct benefit on one company. Eligible actions explicitly include development/implementation of digital platforms for knowledge transfer, pilot demonstrators, technology roadmapping, open-innovation/co-creation environments and structured matching between scientific supply and company needs.
opportunities.project_fit: Relevant as a partner-led route rather than a direct company grant. CCR/news-analysis/media-literacy tooling and broader web/app/AI/data capability could be packaged as a digital platform, demonstrator or experimentation component inside a CTI/CoLAB-led knowledge-transfer action, provided outputs are collective and openly available. Best used to approach digital-oriented CTIs/CoLABs, not as an SME applicant route.
opportunities.recommended_role: technical co-developer / platform work-package contributor / company cooperation partner to a CTI or CoLAB lead
opportunities.next_action: Identify 3–5 recognised CTI/CoLAB leads in Norte/Centro with digital, AI, software or knowledge-transfer focus and pitch a collective digital-platform/demonstrator work package; confirm procurement/subcontracting versus cooperation structure before committing budget.
